md_name: Freshwater Lake 18S rRNA Community Sequencing Workflow
md_description: This DAG represents the acquisition and processing of 18S rRNA amplicon sequencing data from freshwater lake microbial communities sampled across depths, zones, seasons, and geographic regions. It tracks physical sample collection, nucleic-acid preparation, sequencing, and computational derivation of community feature tables and taxonomy-based summaries used to study environmental and seasonal drivers of eukaryotic microbial diversity.

freshwater_lake_water_sample.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic sample identity and provenance fields for the collected freshwater water sample: where it came from, when it was collected, and the environmental context that defines the sample itself (lake, region, depth, zone). I excluded downstream process details such as filtration, DNA extraction, sequencing, read quality, or computed community outputs, because those belong to later nodes. I also avoided fields that would duplicate identifiers already reserved at the root entity level elsewhere in the DAG; instead I focused on sample-specific location and collection metadata needed to interpret the sample in this freshwater lake 18S rRNA study.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the collected water sample; use a stable string such as 'LL01_D02_EP_2024-06-15_S01' that can be traced across all downstream workflow steps. This is the primary sample identifier and should be assigned at collection.
Name of the freshwater lake from which the water sample was collected; record the official or project-defined lake name at sampling time.

Geographic region or basin containing the lake sample location, recorded as a project-defined string such as 'Upper Midwest' or 'Northern Basin'. This describes the sample origin at the regional scale, not the instrument or processing context.
Date the water sample was collected in the field, recorded in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD), e.g. '2024-06-15'. Used to relate the sample to seasonal dynamics.

Water column depth at which the sample was collected, measured in meters at the sampling point; typical freshwater lake ranges are 0 to 100+ m depending on lake depth. Use the actual depth used for this sample, e.g. 0.5, 5.0, 20.0.
Lake zone from which the sample was collected, describing the within-lake habitat/stratum at collection time. Use one of the allowed categorical values below.

Field method used to obtain the water sample, recorded as the sampling approach applied at collection time (for example, grab sample, integrated water sample, or depth-discrete sample). This describes the sample itself, not later concentration or filtration steps.

Volume of lake water collected for this sample at the time of field collection, in liters; typical values are often 0.5 to 20 L depending on biomass and protocol. Record the actual collected volume used for downstream processing.
Free-text notes on the physical field context of the sample at collection time, such as visible turbidity, algal blooms, ice cover, or unusual conditions affecting interpretation of the sample.

filtration_concentration.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only how the filtration/concentration was performed and the key operational parameters needed to reproduce biomass capture. I focused on protocol settings such as filter type, pore size, processed volume, vacuum/pressure, duration, and temperature, plus a simple output quality indicator for the retained biomass. I excluded sample provenance fields (those belong to the upstream water sample entity), downstream DNA/capture outputs (those belong to the microbial pellet entity), and instrument/software agent details because this process is described as researcher-operated rather than software-driven.

md_schema.descr: Biomass concentration approach used on the lake water sample at the filtration step; specify the operational mode applied to retain microbial biomass for DNA extraction.
Nominal pore size of the filter used during concentration, in micrometers, measured as part of the filtration setup; typical values are 0.2 to 5.0 µm for microbial biomass retention.
Material of the filtration membrane or cartridge used during biomass concentration, recorded at the time of processing (for example, polyethersulfone or cellulose nitrate).
Volume of water processed through the concentration step, in liters, measured during the filtration workflow; use the actual sample volume applied to the filter or concentrator.

Applied vacuum or transmembrane pressure used during filtration, in kilopascals, recorded while the sample is being concentrated. Typical values depend on the system and are often within 10 to 90 kPa.
Elapsed time for the filtration or concentration step, in minutes, measured from start of processing until the biomass was retained and the sample was complete.
Ambient or processing temperature during filtration, in degrees Celsius, recorded at the time of concentration because temperature can affect biomass handling and downstream DNA integrity.

Operational indicator of how much biomass was retained after filtration, recorded as a qualitative assessment or relative yield at the end of the concentration step. Use the allowed values below to indicate the observed outcome.

concentrated_microbial_pellet.reasoning: This is an Entity node representing the biomass product after filtration and before DNA extraction, so I included only intrinsic properties of the concentrated pellet itself: what it is, how much material was recovered, and basic storage/handling provenance needed to interpret downstream extraction. I excluded filtration protocol settings because those belong to the upstream process node, and I excluded DNA yield or extraction chemistry because those belong to the downstream extraction process/entity. I also avoided repeating sample-origin identifiers already captured at the root sample entity.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the concentrated microbial pellet or biomass aliquot produced from the lake water sample; use a stable string such as 'LL01_D02_EP_2024-06-15_pellet1'. This identifies the retained biomass prior to DNA extraction.

Wet mass of the concentrated biomass pellet, in milligrams, measured after filtration/concentration and before any lysis or extraction steps. Typical values depend on biomass load and filtration volume and may range from <1 mg to hundreds of mg.
Storage temperature of the concentrated pellet immediately after collection/concentration and before DNA extraction, in degrees Celsius; record the actual holding temperature such as 4, -20, or -80.
Duration that the concentrated pellet was stored before DNA extraction, in hours, measured from completion of filtration to start of extraction.
Preservation or storage medium used for the concentrated biomass pellet prior to nucleic acid extraction, recorded as the actual buffer or preservative applied if any.

Qualitative description of the biomass pellet appearance immediately after concentration, such as visible, faint, turbid, or compacted; this helps document whether a recoverable biomass pellet was obtained for extraction.

dna_extraction.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the extraction protocol parameters and performance indicators for converting concentrated biomass into purified DNA. The fields cover extraction chemistry, kit/protocol, lysis conditions, elution details, input material amount, and a simple output quality indicator so downstream users can judge whether the extract is suitable for 18S amplicon library preparation. I excluded pellet properties because those belong to the upstream entity, and I excluded DNA yield/product properties because those belong to the downstream extracted DNA entity. I also did not repeat any identifiers or collection metadata already captured on the sample entity.

md_schema.descr: Commercial kit or in-house protocol used to extract DNA from the concentrated microbial biomass, recorded as the method applied during this process step. Use the exact kit name when available, for example a soil or environmental DNA extraction kit.

Cell lysis approach used during DNA extraction, recorded at the time of extraction (for example bead beating, enzymatic lysis, chemical lysis, or combined methods). This describes how biomass was disrupted before purification.
Mass of concentrated microbial biomass input to the extraction, in milligrams, measured immediately before lysis/purification. Typical values depend on the filtered biomass and pellet recovery.
Time spent in the lysis phase of the DNA extraction protocol, in minutes, measured during the extraction process from lysis start to completion.
Final elution volume used to recover purified DNA from the extraction column or bead cleanup, in microliters, measured at the end of the protocol.

Amount of DNA recovered from the extraction step, in nanograms, measured after purification and before library preparation. Typical yields may range from sub-ng to several hundred ng depending on biomass and protocol.
DNA purity metric based on absorbance at 260/280 nm, measured on the extracted DNA after purification. Typical values near 1.8 indicate relatively pure DNA.

Simple outcome flag indicating whether the extraction produced usable DNA for downstream amplicon library preparation. This is a process-level quality indicator, not a property of the DNA entity itself.

extracted_dna.reasoning: I removed the colliding field dna_purity_ratio_260_280 because it had already been generated earlier in the DAG. The remaining fields stay within the Entity territory of the extracted DNA node: intrinsic identity, concentration/yield, alternate purity metric, integrity, and storage conditions. I did not add any process, capture, or downstream library-prep fields, and I avoided repeating upstream sample or extraction metadata.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the purified DNA extract; use a stable string such as 'LL01_D02_EP_2024-06-15_DNA1'. This identifier links the extract to its source biomass and downstream library preparation.

Concentration of the purified DNA extract, in nanograms per microliter, measured after extraction and prior to amplicon library preparation. Typical environmental DNA values may range from <0.1 to >50 ng/µl.
Total recovered DNA mass, in nanograms, calculated from concentration and elution volume or measured directly after extraction. Record the value for the final extract used as template.
DNA purity ratio measured from UV absorbance at 260/230 nm after extraction, used to assess salt or organic carryover contamination. Typical values for clean extracts are often around 2.0 to 2.2.
Qualitative assessment of DNA fragmentation or integrity at the time the extract is prepared for library construction. Use the allowed categorical values below.
Storage temperature for the purified DNA extract prior to library preparation, in degrees Celsius; record the actual storage condition such as 4, -20, or -80.
Buffer or solvent used to store the purified DNA extract before 18S rRNA amplification, recorded as the actual solution if known, for example nuclease-free water or TE buffer.

amplicon_library_preparation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the amplification and indexing protocol parameters needed to reproduce the 18S library preparation. I focused on primer choice, target amplicon region, PCR conditions, indexing strategy, cycle count, reaction volumes, and a process-level success indicator. I excluded DNA template properties because those belong to the upstream extracted DNA entity, and I excluded final library file/output properties because those belong to the downstream indexed library entity. I also avoided the previously generated DNA purity metric due to the DAG-wide field collision constraint.

md_schema.descr: 18S rRNA gene region amplified during library preparation, recorded as the specific variable region or locus targeted at PCR setup time (for example V4 or V9).
Forward primer sequence used for 18S amplification, recorded as the exact oligonucleotide sequence applied in the PCR reaction. Use standard DNA base notation, e.g. 'CCAGCASCYGCGGTAATTCC'.
Reverse primer sequence used for 18S amplification, recorded as the exact oligonucleotide sequence applied in the PCR reaction. Use standard DNA base notation, e.g. 'ACTTTCGTTCTTGATYRA'.
Number of PCR cycles used to amplify the 18S target during library preparation, measured as the total cycle number in the amplification program; typical values are often 20 to 35 cycles.
Annealing temperature used in the PCR program for 18S library amplification, in degrees Celsius, recorded at the amplification step; typical values are often 50 to 65 °C depending on primer design.
Total volume of each PCR reaction used to create the amplicon library, in microliters, recorded at the time of library preparation; typical values are often 10 to 50 µl.

Indexing or barcode strategy used to multiplex libraries, recorded during library preparation. Use the allowed categories below to describe whether sample-specific indices were added in one or two PCR steps.
Process-level outcome flag indicating whether the amplification and indexing yielded a sequencing-ready library of acceptable quality for loading onto the sequencer.

indexed_18s_library.reasoning: This is an Entity node representing the finished sequencing-ready library, so I included intrinsic library properties such as library identifier, concentration, fragment size, indexing identity, pooling status, and storage conditions. I excluded PCR and indexing protocol settings because those belong to the upstream library-preparation process, and I excluded sequencing instrument settings because those belong to the downstream capture node. I also avoided any DNA purity or extraction metrics already generated elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the finalized indexed 18S amplicon library; use a stable string such as 'LL01_D02_EP_2024-06-15_LIB1'. This identifies the sequencing-ready library prior to instrument loading.

Concentration of the indexed library, in nanograms per microliter, measured after final cleanup and before sequencing run setup. Typical values depend on the cleanup method and may range from <0.1 to >20 ng/µl.

Average or modal fragment size of the amplified 18S library, in base pairs, measured after amplification and indexing. Typical amplicon library sizes often fall between 200 and 800 bp depending on the target region and adapters.
Sample-specific index or barcode sequence associated with this library, recorded as the exact tag used to multiplex the sample. Use standard nucleotide sequence notation if known.

Indicates whether the library was kept as an individual preparation or combined into a pooled sequencing set prior to loading. This describes the library entity itself at the time it is transferred to sequencing.
Storage temperature for the finalized library before sequencing, in degrees Celsius; record the actual condition such as 4, -20, or -80.

Whether the final library met internal quality-control criteria for sequencing readiness, based on post-cleanup size and concentration checks. This is an entity-level quality flag, not a process description.

illumina_sequencing_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the instrument session and configuration details for the Illumina sequencing run: hardware identity, run chemistry, read structure, indexing mode, loading concentration, and basic run quality indicators. I excluded sample/library intrinsic properties because those belong to upstream entity nodes, and I excluded raw file properties because those belong to the downstream signal node. I also avoided process software fields because this node is an instrument capture step rather than a computational process.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for the Illumina run, recorded as the hardware vendor at the capture step. For this workflow it should identify the sequencing platform vendor.
Sequencing instrument model used to read the indexed 18S library, recorded at the time of the capture session; for example, a MiSeq-class instrument.
Serial number of the sequencing instrument used for this capture session, recorded from the hardware at run setup. Use the exact machine serial identifier when available.
Sequencing chemistry or reagent kit version used for the run, recorded during instrument setup. This describes the active Illumina run configuration, such as the sequencing kit generation.
Read structure configured for the sequencing run, describing the read lengths and index reads used for the indexed 18S library. Use a format such as '2x300' or '2x250 + i7 + i5'.
Indexing mode selected on the instrument for demultiplexing the library, indicating whether single or dual index reads were collected during the capture session.

Final library loading concentration applied to the sequencer at run setup, in picomoles per liter, recorded as the active instrument loading setting. Typical values depend on platform and library complexity.

Observed cluster density on the flow cell during the sequencing run, in thousands of clusters per square millimeter, measured as a run-quality indicator after image processing. Typical acceptable values are platform-specific and often fall within vendor-recommended ranges.
Run identifier assigned by the instrument software to this sequencing session; use a stable string such as 'RUN_2024_06_15_A'. This links the capture event to the generated raw reads.

raw_fastq_reads.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw data artefact properties of the FASTQ files: file identity, format, size, read counts, base-call dimensions, compression, and storage location/technical quality. I excluded sequencing instrument settings because those belong to the upstream capture node, and I excluded trimming, denoising, or biological interpretation because those belong downstream. I also avoided any sample, DNA, or library identifiers that were already generated on upstream entity nodes, unless needed as file-level linkage metadata.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw FASTQ file produced by the sequencing run, recorded as the exact file label used in storage. This identifies the raw signal artefact prior to any processing.

Storage path or URI for the raw FASTQ file, recorded as the physical or logical location of the data object at rest. Use a reproducible path string such as '/data/run1/sampleA_R1.fastq.gz' or a repository URI.
File encoding format of the raw sequence signal, recorded at the time the file is generated; for this workflow it should indicate whether the file is FASTQ and whether it is compressed.
Size of the raw FASTQ file in bytes, measured from the stored signal artefact. Typical values vary with read depth and read length.
Total number of sequence reads contained in the raw FASTQ file, counted after demultiplexing or instrument export. This is a file-level count of raw reads before filtering.
Length of each raw read in base pairs, as produced by the instrument and captured in the FASTQ signal. For paired-end runs, record the per-read length.
Phred quality score encoding used in the FASTQ file, recorded as a file-format property at the signal stage. Use the allowed values below.
Checksum or hash used to verify file integrity for the raw FASTQ artefact, recorded as a technical quality control field. Use an exact hash string such as MD5 or SHA-256 when available.

read_trimming_and_filtering.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the trimming and filtering protocol parameters and a process-level quality indicator. The fields capture which software was used, what was removed, and the main thresholds that control read retention, because these are the operational details needed to reproduce the preprocessing. I excluded raw FASTQ file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting filtered-read file properties because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided repeating any agent/software fields already generated elsewhere except the process-specific software identity required on operation nodes.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or workflow used for adapter, primer, and quality trimming at this step, recorded as the exact tool name applied to the raw reads.
Version of the trimming software used during preprocessing, recorded at the time the reads were filtered. Use the exact release identifier, for example 'v2.0' or '2024.2'.
Adapter sequence removed from raw reads during trimming, recorded as the exact nucleotide sequence or adapter label used by the trimming workflow.
Primer sequence removed from raw reads during preprocessing, recorded as the exact amplicon primer sequence targeted for removal if applicable.
Minimum per-base quality score threshold applied during trimming/filtering, recorded as the cutoff used to remove low-quality bases. Typical values are often in the range 10 to 30.
Minimum read length retained after trimming and filtering, in base pairs; reads shorter than this threshold were discarded at the preprocessing step.
Maximum expected errors allowed per read during filtering, recorded as the E-value or expected error cutoff used to retain reads. Typical values are often 1.0 or 2.0 for amplicon workflows.
Process-level flag indicating whether trimming and filtering completed successfully and yielded reads suitable for downstream denoising.

quality_filtered_reads.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only the technical properties of the filtered-read artefact: file identity, location, format, size, read counts, read length, and technical loss/quality metrics. I excluded trimming parameters because those belong to the upstream process node, and I excluded denoising or taxonomic interpretation because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating upstream sample/library identifiers except where useful for file-level linkage.

md_schema.descr: Name of the quality-filtered reads file produced after trimming and filtering, recorded as the exact file label used in storage. This identifies the processed signal artefact.
Storage path or URI for the quality-filtered reads file, recorded as the logical or physical location of the processed read artefact.

File format of the quality-filtered reads artefact, recorded after preprocessing. For this workflow the value should indicate whether the file is FASTQ, compressed FASTQ, or another supported sequence file type.
Number of reads retained after trimming and filtering, counted from the processed reads file. This is the post-QC read count available for downstream denoising.

Fraction of input raw reads retained after trimming and filtering, calculated as filtered_read_count divided by raw_read_count. This technical quality metric summarizes preprocessing loss at the signal stage.
Length of each retained read in base pairs after trimming and filtering, measured on the processed reads file. For paired-end data, record the per-read retained length.
Size of the quality-filtered reads file in bytes, measured from the stored artefact after preprocessing.
Checksum or hash for the processed reads file used to verify integrity of the quality-filtered signal artefact, such as MD5 or SHA-256.

denoise_asv_inference.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the denoising/inference algorithm settings and process-level performance indicators for turning quality-filtered reads into ASVs. The fields cover the software used, denoising mode, chimera handling, minimum abundance thresholds, and whether an error model or pooled strategy was applied. I excluded file-level properties of the filtered reads because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting ASV table properties because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating any software-identifying fields beyond what is necessary on a process node, and I did not repeat any fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to infer amplicon sequence variants from filtered reads, recorded as the exact tool applied at this process step.
Version of the denoising software used during ASV inference, recorded as the exact release identifier or build version.
Algorithmic mode used for error correction and ASV inference from quality-filtered reads, recorded during the denoising step.
Chimera handling strategy applied during ASV inference, recorded as the method used to identify and remove chimeric sequences from the filtered reads.

Minimum sequence abundance threshold used to retain inferred ASVs or features during denoising, recorded as the cutoff applied by the inference workflow. Typical values are 1 or higher depending on the method.
Indicates whether denoising was performed independently per sample or using a pooled strategy across samples, recorded at the time of ASV inference.
Process-level outcome flag indicating whether ASV inference completed successfully and produced a usable feature table.

asv_table.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed-result properties of the ASV feature table: table identity, dimensions, sparsity/completeness, abundance totals, inference provenance, and basic computational quality indicators. I excluded denoising algorithm parameters because those belong to the upstream process node, and I excluded taxonomic annotations because those belong to the downstream taxonomic assignment derivative. I also avoided repeating any raw-read or library metadata already defined elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the inferred ASV table, use a stable string such as 'ASV_TABLE_2024_06_15'. This identifies the computed feature matrix produced from denoising.
Number of distinct ASVs/features represented in the abundance table, counted after denoising and dereplication. This is the number of columns/features in the matrix.
Number of samples represented in the ASV table, counted at the time the derivative is produced. This is the number of rows/samples in the matrix.
Sum of all sequence counts across the full ASV table, calculated from the inferred abundance matrix. This provides the total retained signal represented in the derivative.
Fraction of zero entries in the ASV abundance matrix, calculated after inference as an indicator of table sparsity. Values are between 0 and 1, with higher values indicating a sparser matrix.
File or serialization format used to store the ASV abundance matrix, recorded as the computational output format such as BIOM, TSV, CSV, or similar.
Software used to generate or export the ASV table, recorded as the computational tool that produced the derivative object. Use the exact program name when known.
Version of the software used to generate the ASV feature table, recorded as the exact release or version string.

taxonomic_assignment.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the classification workflow details needed to reproduce taxonomic assignment: classifier/database identity, version, target taxonomy rank depth, confidence threshold, and a process-level success indicator. I excluded ASV table dimensions and feature counts because those belong to the upstream derivative, and I excluded the resulting taxonomy labels because those belong to the downstream taxonomic profiles derivative. I also kept software/vendor details on the process node as required for operation nodes, but did not repeat any already-generated field names.

md_schema.descr: Name of the taxonomic classification tool or workflow used to assign taxonomy to representative ASV sequences, recorded as the exact classifier applied during this process step.
Version of the taxonomic classifier used for assignment, recorded as the exact release identifier or build version used at analysis time.
Name of the reference taxonomic database used for classification, recorded at the time taxonomy was assigned. Examples include curated 18S reference databases.
Version or release date of the reference database used for taxonomic assignment, recorded to support reproducibility of the classification results.
Deepest taxonomic rank reported by the classifier for the assigned ASVs, recorded as the intended resolution of the assignment output.
Minimum confidence score required to accept a taxonomic assignment, recorded as the cutoff used by the classifier. Typical values may be between 0 and 1 depending on the software.
Classification approach used to assign taxonomy from representative ASVs, recorded as the algorithmic strategy applied during this process step.
Process-level flag indicating whether the taxonomic assignment completed successfully and produced usable taxonomy calls for downstream analysis.

taxonomic_profiles.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only properties of the computed taxonomic profile output: table identity, number of annotated features, taxonomic resolution, completeness of assignment, abundance summary, and output format. I excluded classifier/database settings because those belong to the upstream taxonomic assignment process, and I excluded community summary statistics because those belong to the downstream community analysis derivative. I also avoided repeating any previously generated fields such as sample identifiers or ASV table identifiers.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived taxonomic profiles table; use a stable string such as 'TAX_PROFILES_2024_06_15'. This identifies the computed ASV-to-taxonomy annotation output.
Number of ASVs/features in the taxonomic profiles table that received a taxonomic annotation at one or more ranks, counted after classification.
Number of ASVs/features that remained unassigned at the chosen reporting depth, counted in the derived taxonomy output. This helps summarize classifier coverage.
Deepest taxonomic rank represented in the derived profiles, describing the granularity of the taxonomic annotation output. Use the allowed values below.
Fraction of ASV features that received a usable taxonomic assignment in the derived profiles table, calculated as annotated_feature_count divided by total_feature_counts from the upstream ASV table.
File or serialization format used to store the taxonomic profiles output, recorded as the computational result format such as TSV, CSV, BIOM, or similar.
Software used to create or export the taxonomic profiles derivative, recorded as the exact analysis tool that assembled the annotated table.
Version of the software used to generate the taxonomic profiles table, recorded as the exact release or version string.

community_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the computational analysis settings and summary-level outputs needed to reproduce the community comparison step. I focused on analysis software, diversity/ordination methods, grouping variables, normalization strategy, and a process-level success indicator. I excluded the underlying ASV and taxonomy table properties because those belong to the upstream derivatives, and I excluded the final summary table/file properties because those belong to the downstream community summary derivative. I also avoided repeating any already_generated fields such as sample identifiers or previously used software/version field names unless needed for this node’s analysis tool identity.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or analysis framework used to integrate the ASV table and taxonomic profiles for community analysis, recorded as the exact tool applied at this process step.
Version of the community analysis software used during the integration step, recorded as the exact release identifier used for reproducibility.
Statistical or ecological method used to summarize community structure at this step, recorded as the primary analysis approach applied to compare samples across lakes, depths, zones, and seasons.
Abundance normalization or rarefaction strategy used before community-level comparison, recorded as the method applied to the ASV data during analysis.
Sample grouping factors included in the analysis, recorded as the ecological and temporal variables used to summarize community structure (for example lake, depth, zone, season).
Distance or dissimilarity metric used for beta-diversity or ordination analyses, recorded when community comparisons are based on pairwise distances. Examples include Bray-Curtis or Jaccard.
Process-level flag indicating whether the community analysis completed successfully and produced usable outputs for downstream summarization.

community_summary.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only properties of the computed community summary output: output identity, summary type, dimension/coverage, key diversity or ordination metrics, grouping scope, and file format. I excluded upstream analysis settings because those belong to the community_analysis process, and I excluded raw ASV/taxonomy properties because those belong to earlier derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating any fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG, especially sample identifiers and software/version fields.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the final community summary derivative; use a stable string such as 'COMMUNITY_SUMMARY_2024_06_15'. This identifies the computed output used for ecological interpretation.
Type of community summary represented by the derivative output, recorded as the main ecological summary produced from the analysis.
Number of samples represented in the community summary output, counted after integration of ASV and taxonomic information.
Number of features, taxa, or aggregated groups represented in the community summary output, counted after community analysis and summarization.
Name of the primary diversity metric or ecological statistic reported in the community summary, recorded as the metric used for comparison across environmental gradients.

Ordination or multivariate method used in the summary output when applicable, recorded as the method underlying the ecological comparison. Use the allowed values below when an ordination-based summary is produced.
Ecological grouping factors summarized in the final community output, recorded as the main variables compared in the derivative (for example lake, depth, zone, season).
File or serialization format used to store the community summary derivative, recorded as the output representation such as CSV, TSV, RDS, or similar.
High-level quality flag indicating whether the final summary output is complete and suitable for interpretation. This is a derivative-level technical assessment, not a process parameter.
